well yeah its likely scattered because its not well formulated in my mind

its quite hard to express what i am trying to say

well yeah its likely scattered because its not well formulated in my mind

the beats or plot points that are important is that:
- a conversation happens within an ethic: there are invisible rules that decide not only whether the conversation is productive
- but also im positing that there is a set of possible conversational principles and that define what is possible or achievable with conversation

.   
   - e.g. i've experienced conversations that caused mania in me and my interlocutor that lasted for hours and was quite unpleasant for us both
   - e.g. i've experienced debates that go nowhere and where the people aren't really interested in mutual discovery but rather take downs and protecting their insecure beliefs
   - e.g. i've experienced conversations that are mutual explorations, and these kinds of conversations operate with different principles that i had to learn, and some of them are counter intuitive and hard for autistic people to understand.
            - e.g. on interesting principle that i think not many people are aware of is what im just gonna call the "don't follow up" principle. which means when someone tells you something you don't question it if you don't have clarity, you allow them to guide you through if there is implied uncertainty in the vibe and if that doesn't happen you both let it die. and the trade off with this principle is that on the negative side, if you did question their utterances you would eventually reach a set of facts about the situation they are conveying that is a different interpretation than the one they gave you, so you are basically getting an "untrue" version of events, but the positive side is you are both exploring an interpretation that aligns with how the person felt and you aren't interested in changing how they feel but rather exploring the computational space that this person's awareness exists in. this is hard to express but yeah its something i've noticed, i didn't explain it well
     - e.g. another principle is to express observations rather than opinions. instead of saying "i think this is whats happening in the world" you say "i saw a post that mentioned this, and i had the experience that there is something off with that framing". so you are closer to the source material instead of injecting your interpretations

.

and i read a wiki about a woman trying to formulate principles that characterize a conversational ethic that she calls the cooperative principle

so my mind goes to "well how do you test something like this? it sounds like you are saying 'the sky is blue',"

like one principle is the maxim of quantity. the maxim is "be informative" and it breaks down into "don't say too much and don't say too little"

and hearing that i think "well yeah fucking obviously right? the sky is blue bro"

but then i realized that if you analyze the conversation of someone that is triggered, you can literally see them violate this principle

e.g. when im triggered i tend to not give enough information like:

> A: "have you seen Joe?"
> S: "yeah"
> A: "where is he?"
> S: "i don't know" 
> A: "but you said you saw him"
> S: "yes i've seen him before, he lives here" 
> A: "but did you see him recently?"
> S: "yeah" 
> A: "ok when did you see him?" 
> S: "this morning"
> A: "where did you see him"
> S: "at the pool"

and this entire exchange could have been a one turn conversation (which conforms to the maxim of quantity), and they are rarely patient enough to go through the entire dance, it could have been

> A: "have you seen Joe?"
> S: "i saw him at the pool this morning but i don't know where he is right now"

so i just thought its clever that you can test conversational maxims by comparing different types of conversation

and i think its invisible generally and thats why its interesting to talk about and think about

.

and finally the part that's quite interesting is that ok can you say "western culture actually has a type of conversational ethic which started somewhere in greece and it has these properties" and then you can check "ok this eastern european culture actually doesn't have some of these principles"
e.g. through speaking to my russian friend i learned about "vranyo"

he didn't tell me about it, i just realized that when speaking to him that there is a clash or anomaly in the ethic of how we speak, i experienced it as him basically having blatant lies and he knows i know he is lying but i can't do anything about it, i  can't call it out cuz he will talk around it and deny it etc

but he wasn't malicious this is just normal

its a value difference in how truth is treated

truth is a tool not a goal

and there is this concept that a guy that wrote a book on fascism talks about where the leader tells these kinds of lie that don't have the goal of "getting away" with it or trying to "convince" people, they basically don't care who thinks or knows they are lying, they can be blatant, because the goal is simply to provide a story for the loyal followers to adopt

and when the loyal follower adopts it it's like a shiboleth, the more blatant the lie the more its a signal of alliegence

and he said this is what happens when you have a cult of personality, its like you trust the leader and you don't care about the "truth" of the situation 

and he said trump has some of that charactaristics

and the interesting part is the more blatant the lie the more it signals that the follower has skin in the game, the stronger the effect, so its actually GOOD that the lie is blatant, if it was less blatant it would actually not be serving its purpose
and this doesn't seem fundamentally depraved?

the vranyo thing? i think its just an ethic

like the disadvantage of the person that cares about the truth in the sense that they dislike lying is that they can't utilize lies 

like you could for example lie for a good cause, and thats what they think they are doing, they are basically just using truth like a tool rather than something to be worshiped
and i kinda see their point
there are disadvantages to worshiping truth
but yes i don't like it and couldn't adapt to it myself

.

and i also realized that shiboleth's like these are quite alluring, i introspected in myself and i realized that e.g. liberal women in america on tiktok that are saying "we want sharia law here", they are basically enacting a shiboleth, they kinda know that what they are doing is destructive to their host but its a signal of alliegence within a group

they are conspiring

and i realized conspiring with people is very alluring

who hasn't had this ingroup type of feeling like "yeah we know its wrong but we normalize it and stand together"

like it happens in mundane ways and crazy ways

the more mundane idea is e.g. just going to go smoke at school during break or whatever

or having a cheat meal together while on a diet

or whatever

so yeah i think there is something to formalizing conversational ethics and finding ways to test it by proxy and seeing how dialing different principles cause differences in what actually happens to social contracts and phenomenology etc
something is fundamentally confusing to me about... all of this. all of it.

i spoke to a guy that lives in my building

and the bullshit he has to deal with, it makes me depressed

like i sat in the gym for a while and just felt sad about the world for a while

and this is while im feeling quite negative about not being close to any of my family members, like my annual grieving

im quite surprised that negativity has depth too

i always thought yeah obviously the positive spectrum of human experience has infinite depth

and i always thought the negative end of the spectrum is quite shallow

but im learning that sadness and pain can be quite deep

the last time i was heartbroken was like 10-15 years ago

and it's more like physical pain than depression

and it gets worse, like it turns into other experiences that are quite unpleasant

like being disappointed is not the same as being heartbroken, it's less intense, but i would say its more deeply unsatisfying
would me saying something about this be useful at all to you?

just pointing out im in a certain attractor atm

and yes, it sucks.

im not used to it being a constant thing
after like a day i started feeling "ok the novelty is wearing off and  its turning into something i can't romanticize"
in my experience depression is more something that has respite, there are better days and worse days, but with pain it doesn't seem to let up a lot
yeah. after a few years you become an actively worse person
eventually you stop being capable of processing positivity.

Christianity is many things

and one of the main things that it is is a sign system

it is a language

but it's a language that exists somewhere on the spectrum between verbal and dancing

it is something you "speak" using words and also using actions, not as sperate things but as a part of one sign system

and I'm starting to understand the language, to keep pushing the metaphor I'd say I'm between the first two stages (see image below)

e.g. why we use the term God and why we have things like original sin and why there is a central figure that you try to imitate are all concepts that are intuitively becoming understandable to me now, there is a clarity

and the interesting thing about conceptualizing it this way is I'm still fully a secular rationalist, I don't have to adopt the ontology of Christianity to speak the language and benefit from it in the same way that learning math opens up a world of academic papers that were inaccessible to you before

if you don't conceptualize religion as a language then it is basically impossible for you to open the black box, if you even have the sense to know that religion is a black box (and most rationalists literally don't even understand that religion is a black box, they think dismissing something is the same thing as explaining it)
